questions.question: What is the botanical name of mango?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mangifera indica**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mangifera indica is the botanical name of mango**__.

 __
 
• In this name, Mangifera represents the genus while indica is a particular species.
 
 
 
• **Scientific name**
 
 
• This system was given by Carolus Linnaeus.
 
• Each name has two components – the Generic name and the specific epithet.
 
• This system of providing a name with two components is called Binomial nomenclature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monoon longifolium **is an Asian small tree species in the family Annonaceae. Common names include false Ashoka, the Buddha tree, the Indian mast tree, and the Indian fir tree.
 
• **Cocos nucifera **is a Coconut tree. It is a tall tree that is native to tropical islands in the western Pacific. 
 
• **Casuarina **is a nitrogen-fixing tree through symbiotic relationship with an actinomycete called Frankia. Common names include coast sheoak, beach casuarina, beach oak, beach sheoak, beach pine, whistling tree, etc.

questions.question: Who among the following economists formulated the Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility (DMU)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**HH Gossen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **HH Gossen formulated the Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility (DMU)**__.

 __
 
• He formulated this law in 1854.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Marginal Utility **is the change in total utility due to a one-unit change in the level of consumption.
 
• **Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility**
 
 
• It states that as** a person consumes an item or a product, the satisfaction or utility that they derive from the product declines as they consume more and more of that product.**
 
• In other words, the additional utility gained from an increase in consumption decreases with each subsequent increase in the level of consumption.
 
 
 
• **Demand curves **are downward-sloping in microeconomic models since each additional unit of a good or service is put toward a less valuable use.
 
• Marketers use the law of diminishing marginal utility because they want to keep marginal utility high for products that they sell.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first to conclude that in vacuum all objects fall with the same acceleration g and reach the ground at the same time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galileo Galilei**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galileo Galilei was the first to conclude that in vacuum all objects fall with the same acceleration g and reach the ground at the same time**__.
 
• **The acceleration of the object equals the gravitational acceleration**.
 __
 
• The mass, size, and shape of the object are not a factor in describing the motion of the object.
 
• So all objects, regardless of size or shape, or weight, free fall with the same acceleration.
 
• In a vacuum, a feather falls at the same rate as a ball.
 
• The remarkable observation that all free-falling objects fall with the same acceleration was first proposed by Galileo Galilei.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Galileo conducted experiments using a ball on an inclined plane to determine the relationship between the time and distance traveled.**

 
 
• He found that the distance depended on the square of the time and that the velocity increased as the ball moved down the incline.
 
• The relationship was the same regardless of the mass of the ball used in the experiment.
 
• The experiment was successful because he was using a ball for the falling object and the friction between the ball and the plane was much smaller than the gravitational force.

questions.question: Which one of the following element is Monatomic unit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gold is a Monatomic unit**__.

 __
 
• Monatomic elements are elements that are stable as single atoms.
 
• For an element to be stable by itself, it must have a stable byte of valence electrons.
 
• The atomic number of a monoatomic element is equal to the number of protons in the element.
 
 
 
• Under standard temperature and pressure conditions, the monatomic elements are the noble gases helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, and radon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gold is the most malleable and ductile metal.**

 
 
• **Symbol: Au**
 
• **Atomic no.: 79**
 
• It is a soft metal and is usually alloyed to give it more strength.
 
• It is a good conductor of heat and electricity and is unaffected by air and most reagents.
 
• The most common gold compounds are auric chloride (AuCl₃) and chloroauric acid (HAuCl₄).

questions.question: Which of the following does **NOT **figure among the main functions of the root system of a plant?

options.text: Absorption of water from the soil
Absorption of mineral from the soil
Providing a proper anchorage to the plant parts
Supply of food to plant parts

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supply of food to plant parts**__.

__
 
• **The supply of food to plant parts is not the main function of the root system of a plant**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Plants have specialized organs that help them survive and reproduce in a great diversity of habitats. The major organs of most plants include roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• Roots are important organs in all vascular plants.
 
 
• Most vascular plants have two types of roots: primary roots that grow downward and secondary roots that branch out to the side.
 
• Together, all the roots of a plant make up a root system.
 
 
 
• A root is a complex organ consisting of several types of tissue. The structure of roots helps them perform their primary functions, which are-
 
 
• **Absorbing water and minerals**
 
 
• Thin-walled epidermal cells and root hairs are well suited to absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil. The roots of many plants also have a mycorrhizal relationship with fungi for greater absorption.
 
 
 
• **Anchoring and supporting the plant**
 
 
• Root systems help anchor plants to the ground, allowing plants to grow tall without toppling over. A tough covering may replace the epidermis in older roots, making them ropelike and even stronger.
 
 
 
• **Storing food**
 
 
• In many plants, ground tissues in roots store food produced by the leaves during photosynthesis. The bloodroot stores food in its roots over the winter.

questions.question: As per Article _______ of the Constitution of India, English is the official language for all the high courts in the country.

questions.question: The story of Maynamati and Gopichandra is a part of which of the following literary works?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nath literature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The story of Maynamati and Gopichandra is a part of Nath literature**__.
 
• Maynamati-Gopichandrer Gan is the story of Queen Maynamati and her husband, Manik Chandra, that propagates yoga guidelines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Nath Literature**

 
 
• It is a **branch of medieval Bangla literature.**
 
• It is based on the Nath cult or yoga-sadhana.
 
• The main god of the Naths is shiva, who is also called Adinath.
 
• The five Nath siddhas (or enlightened)- Minanath, Goraksanath, Hadipa, Kanupa and Chauranginath, are described as having been born from different parts of the body of Adinath.
 
• Nath literature was of two types, didactic and narrative.
 
• Didactic literature was in the form of doha, prahelika or chara, where secrecy was observed with the abundant use of code words and sentences.
 
• Narrative Nath literature was based on legends and stories about the siddhas. The aim of the stories was to attract people to the cult.

questions.question: Yerla, Warna and Dindi are tributaries of the ______ river system.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yerla, Warna, and Dindi are tributaries of the Krishna river system**__. 
 
• **Krishna river**
 __
 
• **It originates in the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar in the state of Maharashtra.**
 
• It flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh. Krishna Basin extends nearly 8% of the total geographical area of the country.
 
• The river has a number of tributaries which include Tungabhadra as the principal tributary and others are Mallaprabha, Koyna, Bhima, Ghataprabha, Yerla, Warna, Dindi, Musi, and Dudhganga.
 
• Nagarjuna Sagar Dam on the Krishna river is the world’s tallest masonry dam (124 meters).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kaveri river**

 
 
• It rises at Talakaveri on the Brahmagiri range (Karnataka) in the Western Ghats.
 
• It is the largest river in the state of Tamil Nadu and the third largest river after Godavari and Krishna in South India.
 
 
 
• **Godavari river**
 
 
• It originates from the Trimbak Plateau in the Nashik District of Maharashtra.
 
• It flows eastward across the Deccan Plateau and drains into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The river is also known as Dakshin Ganga and Gautami.
 
• It is the longest river in Peninsular India.
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra river**
 
 
• It originates under the name of Siang or Dihang, from the Angsi glacier of the Kailash range near the Mansarovar lake.
 
• It enters India west of Sadiya town in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Tributaries: Dibang, Lohit, Siang, Burhi Dihing, Tista, and Dhansari.

questions.question: Which of the following states banned online gaming in October 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Andhra Pradesh banned online gaming in October 2020**__.
 
• The Legislative Assembly adopted the Andhra Pradesh Gaming Amendment Bill-2020.
 
 
• The Andhra Pradesh Gaming Act, 1974 was amended.
 
• With the amendment, the government inserted in the Act “playing an online game for winning money or any other stakes” after the words matka or satta.
 
• Instruments of gaming include cards, dice, gaming, tables or cloth boards, or any other article intended to be used physically or in any virtual or intangible mode, including electronically, as subject means of gaming.
 
• Every offense under this Act is cognizable and non-bailable.
 
 
 
• Online gambling could induce criminal behaviour in society and increase the number of organized crimes such as money laundering and fraud.
 
• Many websites that claim to provide gambling services were not authentic and there were no regulatory measures to check the legitimacy of such sites.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is related to positive economics?

options.text: An increase in money supply implies a price rise in an economy.
Inequalities in the distribution of wealth and incomes should be reduced.
More production of luxury goods is not good for a less developed country.

questions.question: To which neighbouring country was the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) sent in the year 1987?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

__
 
• **Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) was sent to Sri Lanka in the year 1987**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Operation PAWAN**

 
 
• It was the code name assigned to the operation by the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) to take control of Jaffna from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) in late 1987.
 
• It was formed under the India-Sri Lanka Agreement of 1987.
 
• This was to implement the disarmament of the LTTE as a part of the India-Sri Lanka accord.
 
• It was formed under the India-Sri Lanka Agreement of 1987.
 
 
 
• Sri Lanka's newly elected President Ranasinghe Premadasa and V.P. Singh started withdrawing from Sri Lanka after the 1989 governmental election.
 
• The last units of the IPKF left Sri Lanka in March 1990.

questions.question: ______ was conferred the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army in November 2020.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**MM Naravane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MM Naravane was conferred the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army in November 2020**__.

 
 
• He was honored at a special ceremony at 'Sheetal Niwas', the official residence of the President in Kathmandu.
 
• He was also presented with a sword and scroll during the ceremony.
 
• After the ceremony, **General Naravane called on President Bhandari **and expressed his gratitude for the honor accorded to him.
 
• They also discussed measures to further enhance bilateral cooperation.
 
• The practice follows a seven-decade-old tradition of conferring honorary titles on the army chiefs of each other's country.
 
• Commander-in-Chief General KM Cariappa was the first Indian Army Chief to be conferred with this title in 1950.
 
• **Nepalese Army Chief General Purna Chandra Thapa** was also made an Honorary General of the Indian Army by President Ram Nath Kovind at a ceremony in New Delhi.

questions.question: Identify the state animal of Assam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-horned Rhino**__.

__
 
• **The one-horned Rhino is the state animal of Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Great one horned rhino**

 
 
• They are commonly found in Nepal, Bhutan, Pakistan and in Assam, India.
 
• They are confined to the tall grasslands and forests in the foothills of the Himalayas.
 
• Indian Rhinos are brownish-gray in color and are hairless.
 
• They have knobby skin that appears to be armor-plated.
 
• A single horn sits on top of their snout, and their upper lip is semi-prehensile.
 
 
 
• The Indian state of **Assam is home to the largest population of greater-one horned rhinos, with more than 90% in Kaziranga National Park.**
 
• Since 2008, the Indian government, along with WWF and other partners, has translocated 18 rhinos from Kaziranga National Park and Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary to Assam’s Manas National Park on the India-Bhutan border.

questions.question: Mahavira, who was known in Pali literature as Nigantha Nataputta, founded a religion called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jainism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahavira, who was known in Pali literature as Nigantha Nataputta, founded a religion called **Jainism**__. 
 
• **Mahavir Swami was the 24th Tirthankar**.
 __
 
• He is considered the real founder of Jainism.
 
• The lion is a symbol of Mahavir and his discipline is known as Chandrababu.
 
• He was also known as Vardhamana, Jaina, Jitendriya, Kevalin and Arihant.
 
• He was born to Siddhartha and Trisha (Lichchhavi princess) in the early 599 BC at Kundagrama near Vaishali in Bihar.
 
• He died at the age of 72 in Pawapuri which is presently in Bihar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tirthankar**

 
 
• A Tirthankar is referred to as a ‘teaching god’ or ‘Ford Maker’ in Jainism.
 
• In Jainism, it is believed that each cosmic age produces 24 Tirthankaras.
 
• The Tirthankaras in the art are shown in the Kayotsarga pose (dismissing the body).
 
• The 24 Tirthankaras are distinguished from each other by their symbolic colours or emblems.
